findings.finding: Misaligned store emulator writes byte-by-byte across a PMP permission boundary. Bytes before the faulting address are already committed to memory when the fault triggers. The handler redirects the trap to S-mode via sbi_trap_redirect() but the partial writes remain visible, violating PMP region isolation.
Misaligned load emulator reads byte-by-byte across a PMP boundary. On fault at byte i, partial MMIO read side effects from bytes 0..i-1 cannot be rolled back.

S-mode store access fault handler redirects the trap without considering that a decomposable store (CMO, misaligned, or wider-than-XLEN) may have already partially committed visible side effects in allowed PMP regions before the fault.

Trap emulate_store handles FSD/SD/FSW/SW instructions. For FSD (8-byte floating-point store), a single instruction can write across two PMP regions with different permissions, partially committing in the first region before trapping on the second.

Enables Zicbom (ENVCFG_CBCFE + ENVCFG_CBIE) and Zicboz (ENVCFG_CBZE) in menvcfg unconditionally. This grants S-mode the ability to issue CBO instructions (cbo.zero, cbo.clean, cbo.flush, cbo.inval) that are decomposable and can span adjacent PMP regions with differing permissions.

Smepmp configure programs M-only PMP regions with MML=0, then sets MML=1 to enforce Smepmp encoding. No fence between the last region write and the MML set. A speculative memory access initiated before the MML write could resolve under the old encoding, bypassing Smepmp.

Post-PMP-configuration fence only issues sfence.vma (TLB invalidation) but does NOT issue a data cache flush. PMP translations can be cached alongside virtual address translations. A store speculatively performed under old PMP permissions may remain cached and become visible later under new PMP permissions.

PMP unconfigure iterates all entries and disables non-firmware entries without any fence or TLB invalidation. Callers rely on a subsequent configure() call to issue the fence. If unconfigure is ever called without configure, stale PMP translations persist indefinitely.

Domain context switch modifies domain-assignment atomics, PMP configuration, and CSR state in three sequential phases without a unified barrier. Another hart observing the assigned_harts bitmask could see the domain switch but still operate under stale PMP entries. The per-phase synchronization does not compose into end-to-end ordering.

On non-retentive suspend resume, restores menvcfg (including CBIE/CBZE bits enabling S-mode CBO) before the warm-resume path re-programs PMP. The ordering means CBO instructions are executable through a partially-configured PMP if S-mode were entered prematurely between menvcfg restore and PMP configure.

Warm resume gap: menvcfg restore (enabling S-mode CBO) happens before PMP reprogramming. CBO instructions could execute through partially-configured PMP. The resume_finish path then calls sbi_hart_switch_mode() which transitions to S-mode.

ESWIN platform directly programs PMP entries with bare pmp_set(), bypassing domain-based alignment validation. Adjacent PMP entries have differing permissions at arbitrary-address boundaries. HW prefetchers are enabled immediately after with speculation feeding on the newly-established PMP boundaries.
findings.snippet:
pmp_set(PMP_RESERVED_A, PMP_L, EIC770X_L3_ZERO_REMOTE, log2roundup(EIC770X_L3_ZERO_SIZE));
pmp_set(PMP_RESERVED_B, PMP_L, 0, log2roundup(EIC770X_MEMPORT_LIMIT));

findings.finding: Per-domain PMP configure programs entries with pmp_set() directly. Region merging logic relaxes SURW to SURWX to save entries, changing effective permission semantics at boundaries. No alignment validation ensures boundaries are decomposable-memory-operation-safe. Fence is sfence.vma only.
